To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

electricity market restructuring resulted in a significant shift in the composition of electricity generation capacity, from coal to natural gas, with a reduction in the share of coal in electricity generation.
electricity market deregulations have had significant impacts on electricity generation technology and fuel choices.

(i) electricity market deregulation led to a significant increase in the adoption of natural gas technologies, (ii) electricity market deregulations led to a significant reduction in the adoption of coal technologies, (iii) electricity market deregulators led to an increase in renewable investments, (iv) in states that adopted wholesale markets, high natural prices led to more investment in coal technologies and renewables, and (v) in states with regulated markets, high natural-gas prices led to more coal investments.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of electricity market structure in the adoption of electricity technologies, and the impact of electricity market structure on the environmental consequences of the choice of electricity technologies.
the impact of electricity market restructuring on the adoption of electricity technologies, and the implications for the future of the electricity industry.
the implications of market restructuring on technology choices and the resulting environmental impacts.

market restructuring had an important effect on the technology choices of the electricity industry in the United States.

the market restructuring has resulted in a more rapid adoption of natural gas technologies.
